context: Built against spec revision 3 (Payment saga with lease fencing, Reconciler, Provider call protocol §5-7, Void rule, Customer routes > execute check order) and the handoffs of e2 (ho-mv39qe6x-01666ddf), e3 (ho-mv3aalih-011f4d67), e1 (ho-mv38f42c-010fb379, ho-mv38jhfn-01d2ca04, ho-mv39x6r0-013c5688), c3 (ho-mv2r6nzy-016f73cb), d3 and e5 assumption 5. Post-claim authorization read under the fence, sequential captures in supplier-code order, pause without a send on capture_pending or unknown (F-TR-7), all captured -> executed, lease >= 3 x timeout (config, already enforced and tested)
Reconciler tick in the spec order incl. housekeeping (7-day webhook purge, sessions, login failures, idempotency keys, stale model spend) [reconciler.test.js]
RS-25 lost capture cases [lost-response.test.js], RS-21 PENDING [authorization-pending.test.js], ARCH-22 lost authorize incl. the row-2 clauses (a) and (b) [void-rule-lost-authorize.test.js]
main.js starts the fake approval listener (through app.listen) and the reconciler at startup and every RS_RECONCILE_INTERVAL_MS, and passes createVoidPort({clock}) as voidProvider
completedWork: (1) src/services/saga.js (new): processExecutorId (<hostname>:<pid>:<8 hex>), claimExecution (check order: plan status, reservation active and not past expiry, pending/approved/unknown-prev-approved -> AUTHORIZATION_PENDING, any operation not authorized -> AUTHORIZATION_MISSING, any order not confirmed -> COMMITMENT_MISSING, stored expiry <= now + margin -> AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED with the void rule committed before the 409; one BEGIN IMMEDIATE; conditional UPDATE; reservation consumed with consume ledger rows written locally because ledger.js has no consume; one capture intent per order; audit ok / denied), createSaga (begin/start/idle/stop, autoRun flag, runs keyed by plan and epoch), step 2 (getAuthorization per operation under G with a lease renewal before each read; a failed read pauses), step 3 (sequential, startCall with a guard = G(now) + operation authorized + earlier operations captured + lease_epoch stamped on the call; recordCall with apply = capture mapping and fence = epoch; pause when the first non-captured operation is capture_pending/unknown or a retryable answer is backing off; the saga re-reads after the call and accepts captured by a webhook), step 4 (executed, lease_until NULL), step 5 compensation (one transaction under G: CAPTURE_FAILED | AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED, reservation consumed -> reconciling, cancel_requested_at on every open operation, queued captures cancelled, voids and refunds queued, then sent), queueRefundWhenCancelled (the compensation hook for captured), releaseIfSettled (reconciling -> released with restock rows; escalation REFUND_FAILED, VOID_FAILED, UNKNOWN_TOO_LONG, PENDING_TOO_LONG). (2) src/services/reconciler.js (new): the nine steps in spec order, createReconciler (tick joins a running tick, start/stop, meta reconciler_last_tick_at / _ms), resolution by reading for authorize, capture, void and refund (unknown) with the resolution hook and compensation hook in the same transaction, polls with the 5-minute back-off, takeover (never while an operation is capture_pending/unknown or the next capture backs off) that starts the saga with the new epoch, backstops (queued authorize of a cancelled operation -> voided locally; captured + cancelled -> refund; authorized + cancelled without a void -> void), drainReplanQueue, housekeeping. (3) src/routes/plans.js: POST /api/plans/:id/execute (202 {claimed:true,plan} / 200 {claimed:false,plan,rescueStatus}). (4) src/app.js: deps.saga, executorId option, app.close() stops the saga. (5) src/main.js: voidProvider real port, reconciler started after the startup retention pass, returned as reconciler / reconcilerStarted / payments; close() stops the reconciler first; d3's close order and signal handling untouched. (6) Tests: execute.test.js 28, lost-response.test.js 9, authorization-pending.test.js 6, void-rule-lost-authorize.test.js 6, reconciler.test.js 21 = 70 passing (ev:ev-mv3tkpcw-015107ae). Failing-first: the tests were written AFTER the code, not before. Mutation proof (scratch copy of the project under the session scratchpad, real tree never mutated; no ev id because the runs were plain node --test in the copy): lease guard without lease_until (1 test fails), result fence removed (killed only after adding the test 'the epoch is a fence of its own'; before it the mutant survived because the send_token fence also refused), stale-intent step disabled (4 fail), CAPTURED treated as CREATED so a capture is sent again (7 fail), takeover ignoring capture_pending/unknown (3 fail), resolution hook removed from the authorize read (1 fail), poll back-off removed (1 fail), webhook purge 7 days -> 1 hour (1 fail), check order MISSING/COMMITMENT swapped (1 fail), refund_failed counted as settled (2 fail), reservation not consumed and compensation without voids (7 fail), step 2 always run on resume (3 fail). Equivalent or masked mutants: removing the supplier-code-order check inside the capture start guard changes nothing observable (the loop already picks the first non-captured operation; it is defense in depth); removing the resolution hook from the pending poll or the abandon path is masked by the reconciler backstop (authorized + cancelled without a void gets one next step 6). A first attempt to run a mutant inside the real tree was refused by the auto-mode classifier ([Security Weaken]); the edit was reverted at once (grep verified) and the mutants were run in the scratch copy instead. Test-code defects found while writing: void clears last_error_code (assertion moved to the call row), a retryable refund leaves the operation refund_pending, a hand-made capture row needs the operation's amount. No production defect was found by a failing test.

It is e6's file; the new execute route is NOT in that list because plan-execute.json and plan-execute-replay.json already have table rows (still skip rows 'not registered yet': e6 should enable them; the real answers match the fixtures' key sets). npm run test:browser passes 8/8 (ev:ev-mv3tok1s-012c36bd).

RS-39 flake reported by the coordinator (ev:ev-mv3t54i6-01a9b844, passes alone ev:ev-mv3t6bo7-015fdd78): the root cause is in test/api/uploads-retention.test.js (d3): it checks the file right after the row is gone while the sweep unlinks after deleting the row. I reduced the load by starting the reconciler's first tick after the startup retention pass; the race itself remains in the test and the orchestrator should route the one-line fix (wait for the file or for retention.started). Both of my full npm test runs passed that test.

Re-plan drain: drainReplanQueue lives in reconciler.js (2 entries per tick, runPlanningFor, failed_drains + 1 and next_attempt_at = now + min(5 min, 15 s x 2^old failed_drains), entries of archived or deleted requests dropped). f1 owns supersession.js and the queue semantics: if f1 wants it elsewhere or the exponent to use the incremented count, it is a one-line change here, but F-PL-3 forbids f1 from editing reconciler.js, so decide before f1 starts. The 'after 5 failed drains the next step is REPLAN' rule is derive.js's and already works from failed_drains.

Stale model-spend rows (FU-22 owner): both the retention sweep (d3) and reconciler housekeeping call gate.settleStale; it is one compare-and-set UPDATE on status = 'reserved', so a row settles once whichever runs first. d3's call was left in place (not my file).

Stock helpers: consume and restock ledger rows are written by local functions in saga.js because services/ledger.js (c3) has no consume/restock function. They follow ledger.js's row format and the SUM(delta) invariant is asserted in the tests; moving them into ledger.js is a later tidy-up.

The webhook route (e3) moves operations without running the compensation hook for captured; the reconciler backstop (step 6) queues the refund on its next tick instead. If e3's file is touched later it should call queueRefundWhenCancelled (exported from saga.js) in the same transaction.

RESERVATION_EXPIRED on execute also runs the expiry pass inline (expireDueReservations) so the answer and the stored state agree: the plan becomes non_executable (RESERVATION_EXPIRED), stock released, voids sent. The spec does not say; it is the same pass the reconciler would run.

A authorization expired/voided found when a void is refused (resolveRejectedVoid, e2) ends as void_failed by the spec's 'anything else' rule; step 2 compensation after an authorization the provider already shows VOIDED ends voided (the void is refused, getAuthorization says VOIDED).

Not covered here by design: the two-OS-process execute test (e6), SIGKILL/SIGSTOP restart and lease-takeover tests with real processes (f4); the in-process fence test uses a second saga identity over the same database, and the freeze hooks were not used. LIVE-DEPENDENT: real PayPal behaviour of final_capture, DUPLICATE_INVOICE_ID on the capture invoice id (rs-so-<id>-cap), AUTHORIZATION_ALREADY_CAPTURED semantics and request-id retention is unverified until test:live-paypal runs (OQ-D5).
Mutation proofs have no ev ids (plain runs in a scratch copy of the project); the list is in completedWork.

NOTES FOR e6/f1/f4: execute answers 202 {claimed:true, plan:{id,status:'executing'}, requestId} or 200 {claimed:false, plan:{id,status}, rescueStatus, requestId}; refusals are 409 PLAN_SUPERSEDED, PLAN_NOT_EXECUTABLE (details.reason), RESERVATION_EXPIRED, AUTHORIZATION_PENDING, AUTHORIZATION_MISSING, COMMITMENT_MISSING, AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED, INVALID_STATE (plan not approved, or approved without any reservation), each audited as denied. Tests drive the saga with h.app.deps.saga (autoRun, start(planId, epoch), idle(), stop(), executorId; createSaga(deps, {executorId}) makes a second identity over the same database) and the reconciler with createReconciler(h.app.deps, {saga}).tick(); a tick starts resumed sagas in the background (await saga.idle()). Tests must install the real void port (h.app.deps.voidRule = createVoidRule({clock, provider: createVoidPort({clock})})) because createApp keeps the recorder as its default. Fault names used: lost_response:<kind> (effect applied), timeout:<kind> (nothing applied), http_429/422/500:<kind>, capture_declined, capture_pending, refund_pending, refund_failed, authorize_pending, authorize_denied, crash_after_return_commit, capture_lands_after_void_intent. For f4 (restart recovery): a stale started intent becomes unknown after 2 x RS_PAYPAL_TIMEOUT_MS (error_code STALE_INTENT); takeover needs lease_until <= now and happens only when no operation is capture_pending/unknown; the resumed saga repeats step 2 when every capture has send_count 0, else resumes at step 3 and re-sends an unknown capture (same key) only after the reconciler restored the operation to authorized by reading. For f1: supersession of an approved plan still goes through ctx.voidRule; the execute claim refuses a superseded plan and a plan whose authorization expiry is inside the margin runs markNonExecutable(AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED) in the refusal's transaction.

lessonDecisions.note: This task builds no hook or guard that maps file writes to a project record or project root: it changes payment saga, reconciler, route and test files only, so the lesson's 'Applies when' conditions (a guard or hook choosing a project root) do not hold.
